body.purpose: Control text and supporting copy; Qt uses platform fallback outside Windows.

narrative.overview:
A multilingual typing tool expressed through a compact, monochrome terminal grammar: clear labels, thin rules, flat surfaces, and direct controls. It borrows the restraint and native-control character of the Cyberghost Omarchy panel while keeping its own visual identity and real Qt behavior. Consolas on Windows and the platform monospace fallback elsewhere give the interface a consistent typographic voice.

The visual language supports one short path: choose a typing mode, enter raw keystrokes, inspect the actual engine preview, then move to preferences or setup when needed. Color remains quiet; the warm amber is reserved for a running state in dark mode. The system palette selects a neutral light or dark set.
keyCharacteristics: Native Qt controls with square corners and thin borders.
Real input and engine output are the primary work surface.

rules.name: The State-Only Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the connected/running status in dark mode; it is not a general action color. Primary actions use the neutral ink treatment.

rules.name: The Type-By-Size Rule
rules.body: Keep the monospace family consistent; create hierarchy through size, weight, and spacing.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce shadow-based depth; separate regions with tonal changes and one-pixel rules.

dos: Do use the system-selected neutral light or dark palette from Theme.qml.
Do use Consolas on Windows and the platform monospace fallback on Linux.
Do keep the typing flow centered on mode, raw keystrokes, and actual transformed output.
Do use native Qt controls and preserve keyboard focus, accessibility names, disabled states, and text selection.
Do express service state in words as well as color.
donts: Don't use amber as a general action color.
Don't add fake terminal commands, CRT effects, glow, or imagery.
Don't replace real Qt controls with decorative mock controls.
